disposition_reason: Uranium measured in 265 groundwater samples from arid western Rajasthan and northern Gujarat (0.6 to 260 µg/L, mean 24.0 µg/L) with modeled ingestion dose and hazard quotient.
disposition_locator: Abstract p. 1; Results p. 3; Table 2 p. 8

study.design: cross-sectional groundwater survey with geochemical modeling
study.origin: India, western Rajasthan and northern Gujarat (Nagaur, Pali, Jalore, Sirohi, Banaskantha, Barmer)
study.method: LED fluorimetry of uranyl complexes (Quantalase LF-2)
lod: detection limit 0.2 ppb; detection range 0.5 to 1000 ppb (p. 2)
study.qa: triplicate analysis; duplicate and standard checks every ten samples; SRM-1643f for trace elements
study.site_context: groundwater used for drinking and irrigation

findings.group: 265 groundwater samples, western Rajasthan and northern Gujarat, India
findings.notes: Water concentration; not converted to µg/kg.

findings.group: 265 groundwater samples, western Rajasthan and northern Gujarat, India
findings.notes: Abstract rounds the mean to 24 µg/L.

regulatory_or_exposure: WHO provisional guideline 30 µg/L and AERB radiological limit 60 µg/L cited by the authors; no BIS limit, p. 2
Lifetime average daily dose 0.011 to 5.24 µg/kg/day, mean 0.47, versus reference doses 0.6 (WHO) and 4.4 (AERB) µg/kg/day; hazard quotient mean 0.78, p. 8
Mean annual ingestion dose 49.30 µSv/y (infants 0 to 6 months) and 56.34 µSv/y (7 to 12 months), p. 8
non_numeric_findings: 69.3% of samples below 30 µg/L, 27.3% 30 to 60, 3% 60 to 100, 0.38% above 100 µg/L (p. 3); abstract states 30% exceeded 30 µg/L.
Carnotite dissolution, water-rock interaction and evaporation identified as main enrichment processes; uranyl tricarbonate predominant modeled species (pp. 8, 10).
